claim: TMEM120A is a novel membrane protein highly conserved in vertebrates.
source: TMEM120A, also named as TACAN, is a novel membrane protein highly conserved in vertebrates
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract without specific experimental support in this manuscript.

claim: TMEM120A was recently proposed to be a mechanosensitive channel involved in sensing mechanical pain.
source: TMEM120A, also named as TACAN, is a novel membrane protein highly conserved in vertebrates and was recently proposed to be a mechanosensitive channel involved in sensing mechanical pain.
evidence: This claim references prior work proposing TMEM120A as a mechanosensitive channel, supported by citation to Beaulieu-Laroche et al., 2020.

claim: The cryo-EM structure of human TMEM120A was determined to 3.2 Å resolution.
source: The single-particle cryo-EM structure of TMEM120A dimer was determined to the resolution of 3.2 Å
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental cryo-EM data acquisition and processing described in the methods and results.

claim: TMEM120A forms a tightly packed dimer.
source: Here we present the single-particle cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structure of human TMEM120A, which forms a tightly packed dimer
evidence: This is supported by structural data from cryo-EM analysis showing dimeric assembly.

claim: TMEM120A dimerization is mediated by extensive interactions involving the N-terminal coiled coil domain (CCD), the C-terminal transmembrane domain (TMD), and the re-entrant loop between the two domains.
source: which forms a tightly packed dimer with extensive interactions mediated by the N-terminal coiled coil domain (CCD), the C-terminal transmembrane domain (TMD), and the re-entrant loop between the two domains
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis showing specific interaction regions in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The TMD of each TMEM120A subunit contains six transmembrane helices (TMs).
source: The TMD of each TMEM120A subunit contains six transmembrane helices (TMs)
evidence: This is directly observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: TMEM120A has no clear structural feature of a channel protein.
source: The TMD of each TMEM120A subunit contains six transmembrane helices (TMs) and has no clear structural feature of a channel protein.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural analysis showing absence of ion conduction pathway.

claim: The six TMs of TMEM120A form an α-barrel with a deep pocket where a coenzyme A (CoA) molecule is bound.
source: the six TMs form an α-barrel with a deep pocket where a coenzyme A (CoA) molecule is bound
evidence: This is supported by cryo-EM structural data showing the α-barrel architecture and bound CoA ligand.

claim: TMEM120A shares structural features with elongase for very long-chain fatty acids (ELOVL) despite low sequence homology.
source: some structural features of TMEM120A resemble those of elongase for very long-chain fatty acids (ELOVL) despite the low sequence homology between them
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison showing similar 6-TM barrel architecture between TMEM120A and ELOVL7.

claim: TMEM120A may function as an enzyme for fatty acid metabolism, rather than a mechanosensitive channel.
source: pointing to the possibility that TMEM120A may function as an enzyme for fatty acid metabolism, rather than a mechanosensitive channel
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on structural similarities to ELOVL7 and absence of channel features.

claim: TMEM120A was initially identified as a nuclear envelope transmembrane protein (NET) by proteomics and was originally named as NET29.
source: TMEM120A was initially identified as a nuclear envelope transmembrane protein (NET) by proteomics and was originally named as NET29
evidence: This is supported by citations to Malik et al., 2010 and Schirmer et al., 2003.

claim: TMEM120A is preferentially expressed in adipose and plays an important role in adipocyte differentiation.
source: It was suggested to be preferentially expressed in adipose and plays an important role in adipocyte differentiation in an earlier study
evidence: This is supported by citation to Batrakou et al., 2015.

claim: Adipocyte-specific Tmem120a knockout mice cause disruption of fat-specific genome organization and yield a latent lipodystrophy pathology similar to lamin-linked human familial partial lipodystrophy type 2 (FPLD2).
source: adipocyte–specific Tmem120a knockout mice cause disruption of fat-specific genome organization and yield a latent lipodystrophy pathology similar to lamin-linked human familial partial lipodystrophy type 2 (FPLD2)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Czapiewski et al., 2021.

claim: TMEM120A (renamed to TACAN) was shown to be expressed in the plasma membrane of a subset of sensory neurons and function as a mechanosensitive channel involved in sensing mechanical pain.
source: TMEM120A, renamed to TACAN, was shown to be expressed in the plasma membrane of a subset of sensory neurons and function as a mechanosensitive channel involved in sensing mechanical pain
evidence: This is supported by citation to Beaulieu-Laroche et al., 2020.

claim: The authors were unable to reproduce the mechanosensitive activity of TMEM120A expressed in HEK293 or CHO cells.
source: we were unable to reproduce the mechanosensitive activity of TMEM120A expressed in HEK293 or CHO cells
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data from patch-clamp recordings in HEK293 and CHO cells.

claim: The authors did not observe any mechanosensitive channel activity in giant liposome patching using TMEM120A protein reconstituted into lipid vesicles.
source: nor did we observe any mechanosensitive channel activity in giant liposome patching using TMEM120A protein reconstituted into lipid vesicles
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data from giant liposome patch-clamp experiments.

claim: TMEM120A shares several common features with the recently determined ELOVL7 structure.
source: TMEM120A shares several common features with the recently determined ELOVL7 structure
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison and citation to Nie et al., 2021.

claim: ELOVL7 is a member of very long-chain fatty acid (ELOVL) family elongases important for the biosynthesis of very long-chain fatty acids.
source: ELOVL7 structure (Nie et al., 2021), a member of very long-chain fatty acid (ELOVL) family elongases important for the biosynthesis of very long-chain fatty acids
evidence: This is established knowledge about ELOVL7 supported by citations.

claim: ELOVL elongases (ELOVL1-7) are endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membrane enzymes that catalyze a condensation reaction between a long-chain acyl-coenzyme A (CoA) and malonyl-CoA to produce a 3-keto acyl-CoA, free CoA, and CO2.
source: The ELOVL elongases (ELOVL1-7) are endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membrane enzymes that catalyze a condensation reaction between a long-chain acyl-coenzyme A (CoA) and malonyl-CoA to produce a 3-keto acyl-CoA, free CoA, and CO2
evidence: This is established knowledge about ELOVL enzymes supported by multiple citations.

claim: The condensation reaction catalyzed by ELOVL elongases is the first step in the four-step elongation process of very long-chain fatty acids.
source: which is the first step in the four-step elongation process of very long-chain fatty acids
evidence: This is established knowledge about fatty acid elongation supported by citations.

claim: Similar pressure-evoked currents were observed in both control cells (without transfection) and HEK293 cells expressing TMEM120A.
source: Similar pressure-evoked currents were observed in both the control cells (without transfection) and HEK293 cells expressing TMEM120A (Figure 1a).
evidence: This is supported by patch-clamp recording data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: Pressure-evoked currents in HEK293 cells were likely from the endogenous Piezo1 channel.
source: These pressure-evoked currents were likely from the endogenous Piezo1 channel
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that no pressure-elicited channel activity was observed in Piezo1 knockout HEK293 cells.

claim: No pressure-elicited channel activity was observed when Piezo1 knockout (P1KO) HEK293 cells were used for TMEM120A expression and recordings.
source: no pressure-elicited channel activity was observed when Piezo1 knockout (P1KO) HEK293 cells were used for TMEM120A expression and recordings (Figure 1b)
evidence: This is supported by patch-clamp recording data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: Similar pressure-evoked background currents were observed in both control cells and CHO cells expressing TMEM120A.
source: the same pressure-evoked background currents were observed in both the control cells and CHO cells expressing TMEM120A (Figure 1c)
evidence: This is supported by patch-clamp recording data shown in Figure 1c.

claim: No mechanosensitive channel activity was observed when proteoliposomes with a low protein-to-lipid ratio (1:500, w:w) were used in patch-clamp recordings.
source: No mechanosensitive channel activity was observed when proteoliposomes with a low protein-to-lipid ratio (1:500, w:w) were used in our patch-clamp recordings.
evidence: This is supported by giant liposome patch-clamp experimental data.

claim: Some transient currents were observed in patches of proteoliposomes with a higher protein-to-lipid ratio (1:100, w:w).
source: Some transient currents were observed in patches of proteoliposomes with a higher protein-to-lipid ratio (1:100, w:w).
evidence: This is supported by giant liposome patch-clamp experimental data.

claim: Transient currents observed in proteoliposomes with higher protein content were insensitive to pressure and likely resulted from leaky liposome membranes.
source: These currents were insensitive to pressure and likely resulted from leaky liposome membranes when the protein content is high.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that currents were pressure-insensitive and occurred at high protein concentrations.

claim: Human TMEM120A was purified in digitonin detergent as a homo-dimer.
source: solubilized in lauryl maltose neopentyl glycol (LMNG) detergent, and finally purified in digitonin detergent as a homo-dimer
evidence: This is supported by protein purification and structural data.

claim: The EM density map of TMEM120A is of high quality, allowing for accurate model building for residues 8–69, 80–255, and 261–335 for each subunit.
source: The EM density map is of high quality, allowing for accurate model building for the major part of the protein containing residues 8–69, 80–255, and 261–335 for each subunit.
evidence: This is supported by cryo-EM data quality assessment.

claim: Electron density from a bound ligand is clearly visible within each TMEM120A subunit and can be modeled as a CoA molecule.
source: In addition, electron density from a bound ligand is clearly visible within each subunit and can be modeled as a CoA molecule
evidence: This is supported by cryo-EM density map analysis shown in Figure 2f and g.

claim: Each TMEM120A subunit can be divided into two domains: the N-terminal coiled coil domain (CCD) containing CC1 and CC2 helices, and the C-terminal transmembrane domain (TMD) containing six membrane-spanning helices.
source: Each TMEM120A subunit can be divided into two domains: the N-terminal coiled coil domain (CCD) containing CC1 and CC2 helices, and the C-terminal transmembrane domain (TMD) containing six membrane-spanning helices that form an α-helical barrel
evidence: This is directly observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The two domains of TMEM120A are connected by a membrane-penetrating re-entrant loop with a short helix on its tip.
source: The two domains are connected by a membrane-penetrating re-entrant loop with a short helix (named re-entrant helix) on its tip.
evidence: This is directly observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: Multiple membrane protein topology prediction methods implemented in TOPCONS web server predicted that TMEM120A has both N- and C-termini inside (cytosolic side).
source: multiple membrane protein topology prediction methods implemented in TOPCONS web server (https://topcons.net) all predicted that TMEM120A has both N- and C-termini inside (cytosolic side)
evidence: This is supported by computational topology prediction analysis.

claim: The transmembrane α-helical barrel of TMEM120A encloses a deep pocket only open to the inside but completely sealed off from the outside.
source: The transmembrane α-helical barrel enclosed a deep pocket only open to the inside but completely sealed off from the outside
evidence: This is directly observed in the cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 2e.

claim: No discernible ion conduction pathway is present in the TMD of TMEM120A.
source: Thus, no discernible ion conduction pathway is present in the TMD of TMEM120A.
evidence: This is inferred from structural analysis showing the pocket is sealed off from the outside.

claim: Dimerization of TMEM120A starts at CCD where the exceptionally long (~60 residues) CC1 helix forms an anti-parallel coiled coil with CC1 from the neighboring subunit.
source: Dimerization starts at CCD where the exceptionally long (~60 residues) CC1 helix forms an anti-parallel coiled coil with CC1 from the neighboring subunit.
evidence: This is directly observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: CC2 helix has a length of about 1/3 of CC1 and runs anti-parallel to the C-terminal part of CC1, forming a 3-helix bundle with the coiled coil.
source: CC2 helix has a length of about 1/3 of CC1 and runs anti-parallel to the C-terminal part of CC1, forming a 3-helix bundle with the coiled coil
evidence: This is directly observed in the cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 3b.

claim: The re-entrant loop of each TMEM120A subunit is tightly wedged between the two TMDs of the dimer at the internal leaflet of the membrane.
source: The re-entrant loop of each subunit is tightly wedged between the two TMDs of the dimer at the internal leaflet of the membrane.
evidence: This is directly observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The re-entrant loop mediates extensive dimerization interactions through predominantly Van der Waals contacts with the re-entrant loop from the neighboring subunit and the internal halves of TMDs from both subunits.
source: It mediates another set of extensive dimerization interactions through predominantly Van der Waals contacts with the re-entrant loop from the neighboring subunit as well as the internal halves of TMDs from both subunits
evidence: This is directly observed in the cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 3c.

claim: The insertion of the re-entrant loops between the two subunits splits apart the two TMDs at the internal leaflet of the membrane.
source: This insertion of the re-entrant loops between the two subunits splits apart the two TMDs at the internal leaflet of the membrane
evidence: This is directly observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The two TMDs of TMEM120A make direct contact only at the external leaflet of the membrane through some hydrophobic residues at the external parts of TM2, TM3, and TM6.
source: the two TMDs make direct contact only at the external leaflet of the membrane through some hydrophobic residues at the external parts of TM2, TM3, and TM6
evidence: This is directly observed in the cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 3d.

claim: The TMEM120A dimer has an arrowhead-shaped transmembrane region.
source: rendering the TMEM120A dimer with an arrowhead-shaped transmembrane region
evidence: This is directly observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The extensive dimerization of TMEM120A involving virtually every part of the protein implies that the protein has to function as a dimer.
source: Thus, the extensive dimerization of TMEM120A involving virtually every part of the protein implies that the protein has to function as a dimer.
evidence: This is inferred from structural observations of extensive dimerization interactions.

claim: The overall structure of TMEM120A shows no clear feature of a channel protein and has no discernible ion conduction pathway.
source: The overall structure of TMEM120A shows no clear feature of a channel protein and has no discernible ion conduction pathway.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The human ELOVL7 structure (PDB code: 6Y7F) shares the same fold as TMEM120A at the TMD region.
source: identified the human ELOVL7 structure (PDB code: 6Y7F) (Nie et al., 2021) to share the same fold as TMEM120A at the TMD region
evidence: This is supported by DALI structure comparison analysis.

claim: ELOVL7 is an ER membrane enzyme and belongs to ELOVL family elongases that catalyze the condensation reaction step in the elongation process of very long-chain fatty acids.
source: ELOVL7 is an ER membrane enzyme and belongs to ELOVL family elongases that catalyze the condensation reaction step in the elongation process of very long-chain fatty acids
evidence: This is established knowledge about ELOVL7 supported by citation.

claim: ELOVL7 contains seven TMs, and six of them (TMs 2–7) form a 6-TM α-helical barrel that encloses a cytosol-facing pocket where a condensation reaction product of 3-keto acyl-CoA is bound.
source: ELOVL7 contains seven TMs, and six of them (TMs 2–7) form a 6-TM α-helical barrel that encloses a cytosol-facing pocket where a condensation reaction product of 3-keto acyl-CoA is bound
evidence: This is based on the published ELOVL7 structure cited from Nie et al., 2021.

claim: The 6-TM barrel structure of ELOVL7 is strikingly similar to that of TMEM120A (TMs 1–6) with a main-chain RMSD of about 2.5 Å between their barrel-forming 6-TM helices.
source: the 6-TM barrel structure of ELOVL7 is strikingly similar to that of TMEM120A (TMs 1–6) with a main-chain RMSD of about 2.5 Å between their barrel-forming 6-TM helices
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison analysis shown in Figure 4b.

claim: Remote homology at the TMD region between TMEM120A and ELOVL family elongases was detected by the HHpred server for remote protein homology detection and structure prediction.
source: Remote homology at the TMD region between TMEM120A and ELOVL family elongases was also detected by the HHpred server for remote protein homology detection and structure prediction
evidence: This is supported by computational homology detection analysis.

claim: ELOVL elongases contain a highly conserved multi-histidine motif (HxxHH) important for their catalytic activity.
source: ELOVL elongases contain a highly conserved multi-histidine motif (HxxHH) important for their catalytic activity.
evidence: This is established knowledge about ELOVL enzymes.

claim: In ELOVL7 structure, the HxxHH motif is located at the beginning of TM4 with a sequence of HVFHH.
source: In ELOVL7 structure, this motif is located at the beginning of TM4 with a sequence of HVFHH
evidence: This is based on the published ELOVL7 structure cited from Nie et al., 2021.

claim: TMEM120A has a sequence of WVFHH at the equivalent location of the 6-TM barrel (the beginning of TM3), almost identical to the histidine motif of ELOVL7.
source: TMEM120A has a sequence of WVFHH at the equivalent location of the 6-TM barrel (the beginning of TM3), almost identical to the histidine motif of ELOVL7.
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison and sequence analysis shown in Figure 4b.

claim: ELOVL elongases bind CoA derivatives as substrates or products.
source: ELOVL elongases bind CoA derivatives as substrates or products
evidence: This is established knowledge about ELOVL enzymes.

claim: In the ELOVL7 structure a bound 3-keto acyl-CoA product is identified in the deep pocket of the 6-TM barrel.
source: in the ELOVL7 structure a bound 3-keto acyl-CoA product is identified in the deep pocket of the 6-TM barrel
evidence: This is based on the published ELOVL7 structure cited from Nie et al., 2021.

claim: A piece of well-resolved electron density was observed in the pocket of the 6-TM barrel of TMEM120A that fits well with a CoA molecule.
source: we also observed a piece of well-resolved electron density in the pocket of the 6-TM barrel that fits well with a CoA molecule
evidence: This is supported by cryo-EM density map analysis shown in Figure 2f.

claim: The bound ligand in TMEM120A was confirmed to be CoA by biochemical assays.
source: Indeed, this bound ligand was confirmed to be CoA by other biochemical assays
evidence: This is supported by CoA quantification assay and LC-MS/MS analysis.

claim: An assay of 4 mg/ml purified TMEM120A protein sample (~0.1 mM) yielded a CoA concentration of about 0.15 mM in the sample.
source: an assay of 4 mg/ml purified TMEM120A protein sample (~0.1 mM, calculated based on OD280) at various volumes yielded a CoA concentration of about 0.15 mM in the sample
evidence: This is supported by fluorometric CoA assay data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: The measured CoA concentration in TMEM120A sample matches reasonably well to the calculated concentration of CoA with 1:1 protein/ligand ratio.
source: matching reasonably well to the calculated concentration of CoA with 1:1 protein/ligand ratio
evidence: This is inferred from comparison of measured and calculated CoA concentrations.

claim: LC-MS/MS analysis identified both CoA and acetyl-CoA in the TMEM120A protein sample.
source: Thus, LC-MS/MS analysis identified both CoA and acetyl-CoA in our protein sample.
evidence: This is supported by LC-MS/MS data shown in Figure 5b-e.

claim: Peak 1 in LC separation was identified to be acetyl-CoA with a mass (m/z) of 810 Da.
source: Peak 1 was identified to be acetyl-CoA with a mass (m/z) of 810 Da when the two main product ions characteristic of acetyl-CoA fragmentation (303 Da and 428 Da) were used in the scan
evidence: This is supported by LC-MS/MS precursor ion scan data shown in Figure 5c.

claim: Peak 2 in LC separation exhibited a much higher intensity than peak 1 and was detected to have the mass of CoA (m/z = 768 Da).
source: However, peak 2 exhibited a much higher intensity and was detected to have the mass of CoA (m/z = 768 Da) when using the main fragment of CoA at 428 Da in the PI scan
evidence: This is supported by LC-MS/MS precursor ion scan data shown in Figure 5d.

claim: A product ion scan of the 768 Da mass peak yielded the same fragmentation pattern as a CoA standard, confirming the identity of CoA in peak 2.
source: A product ion scan of the 768 Da mass peak yielded the same fragmentation pattern as a CoA standard, confirming the identity of CoA in peak 2
evidence: This is supported by LC-MS/MS product ion scan data shown in Figure 5e.

claim: CoA is likely the main ligand in the purified TMEM120A protein sample.
source: we suspect that CoA is likely the main ligand in the purified protein sample
evidence: This is inferred from structural observation, CoA assay, and LC-MS/MS analysis showing higher intensity of CoA peak.

claim: TMEM120A structure shows no clear feature of an ion channel.
source: While TMEM120A was recently proposed to function as a mechanosensitive channel, its structure shows no clear feature of an ion channel.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis showing absence of ion conduction pathway.

claim: TMDs of both TMEM120A and ELOVL7 contain a 6-TM α-barrel with a very similar topology and architecture.
source: Firstly, TMDs of both proteins contain a 6-TM α-barrel with a very similar topology and architecture.
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison analysis.

claim: Both TMEM120A and ELOVL7 can bind CoA or CoA derivative in the pocket of the 6-TM barrel.
source: Secondly, both proteins can bind CoA or CoA derivative in the pocket of the 6-TM barrel.
evidence: This is supported by structural and biochemical data for TMEM120A and published structure of ELOVL7.

claim: The conserved HxxHH motif important for the catalytic activity of ELOVL elongase is also present at the equivalent location in TMEM120A.
source: Thirdly, the conserved HxxHH motif important for the catalytic activity of ELOVL elongase is also present at the equivalent location in TMEM120A.
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison and sequence analysis.

claim: The similarity between TMEM120A and ELOVL fatty acid elongase may imply enzymatic function of TMEM120A for fat metabolism.
source: its similarity to ELOVL fatty acid elongase is unlikely to be coincidental and may imply enzymatic function of TEME120A for fat metabolism
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on structural and biochemical similarities to ELOVL7.

claim: The final structural model of each TMEM120A subunit contains residues 8–69, 80–255, and 261–335.
source: The final structural model of each subunit contains residues 8–69, 80–255, and 261–335.
evidence: This is based on model building from cryo-EM density map.

claim: Residues 1–7, 70–79, 256–260, and 335–343 of TMEM120A were disordered in the structure.
source: Residues 1–7, 70–79, 256–260, and 335–343 were disordered in the structure.
evidence: This is based on absence of clear density for these residues in the cryo-EM map.
